purpose: Losartan is used to treat high blood pressure, which helps lower your risk of stroke and heart attack. It is also used to protect the kidneys in people who have type 2 diabetes. Sometimes doctors prescribe it to help patients with heart failure.
how_it_works: Your body makes a chemical called angiotensin II that causes your blood vessels to tighten and squeeze, which raises your blood pressure. Losartan blocks the spot where that chemical tries to attach, so your blood vessels stay more relaxed and open. This makes it easier for your heart to pump blood and brings your blood pressure down to a healthier level.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate Losartan very well. Some may notice dizziness, especially when standing up quickly, a stuffy or runny nose, tiredness, or mild back pain. Unlike a similar type of blood pressure medicine called an ACE inhibitor, Losartan rarely causes a dry cough.
warnings: Do not take Losartan if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, or if your potassium levels are high. Avoid potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium unless your doctor says it is okay. Let all your healthcare providers know you are taking this medicine before starting any new medications.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose for adults is 50 mg once a day. Your doctor may adjust your dose to anywhere between 25 mg and 100 mg per day depending on how your blood pressure responds. You can take it with or without food, and it is best to take it at the same time each day to keep it working consistently.
